prompt.context: Your client is a large US-based commercial airline that has lost profitability and market share. The company is under pressure to regain its foothold in the industry and grow its balance sheet.
prompt.question: Can you brainstorm some areas you would like to investigate on behalf of the airline?

clarifying_info.q: What is the timeline for the project?
clarifying_info.a: ASAP – financial investments for the airline typically warrant a payback period of 3 years.

clarifying_info.q: How is the rest of the airline industry performing?
clarifying_info.a: Our client's profitability is declining slightly faster than the industry – but is in line with other airlines within its class of service.

framework: Revenue Opportunities: Ticket Fares, Upselling Opportunities, Cargo Fees, Airline Partnerships, Credit Card Sponsors
Cost Management – Upfront: Airport/Terminal Investment, Equipment Purchase, Initial Staff Training, Marketing & Advertising
Cost Management – Variable: Fuel Costs, SG&A, Maintenance
Other Considerations: Creation of a new domestic hub, Seasonal Risk, Competitive Response, Fuel Efficiency & Prices

questions.prompt: Question 1: The airline has evaluated options and decided to re-examine and add routes. Three routes have been proposed (SEA-MINN, FAY-DALL, NYC-DC). Using Exhibits 1 and 2, what are your key strategic takeaways or pros/cons for each route?
questions.guidance: There is no automatic choice – each route has major tradeoffs. Route 1 (SEA-MINN): Pro – low disruption risk, Pro – quick to establish (3 months); Con – low growth potential, Con – high competition. Route 2 (FAY-DALL): Pro – high growth potential, Pro – low competition, Pro – fastest to establish (2 months); Con – high disruption risk. Route 3 (NYC-DC): Pro – medium growth, Pro – medium disruption risk; Con – high competition, Con – very long setup time (12 months). Strong candidates ask what additional data they would need; interviewer then provides Exhibits 3 and 4.

questions.prompt: Question 2: Using Exhibits 3 and 4, quantify each route's profitability and payback period.
questions.guidance: Combine revenue/ASM and cost/ASM to get CM/ASM. Weight by fill rate and capacity to get passengers, then multiply by distance to get ASM. Scale to annual flights. Divide upfront costs by annual CM to get payback period. Key insight: Route 1 has by far the shortest payback (0.7 years) but lowest annual CM; Route 2 has highest annual CM but mid-range payback (2.1 years) and high risk; Route 3 barely meets the 3-year payback threshold (3.1 years). Weigh shorter payback against risk profile.

math.setup: Step A: Average Passengers = Seats × Fill Rate. ASM = Avg Passengers × Distance. Step B: CM/ASM = Revenue/ASM − Cost/ASM. Step C: Annual CM = CM/ASM × ASM × Flights per day × 300 flying days. Step D: Payback = Total Upfront Cost / Annual CM.
math.answer: Route 1: Annual CM $1,814,400; Payback 0.7 years. Route 2: Annual CM $3,088,800; Payback 2.1 years. Route 3: Annual CM $2,073,600; Payback 3.1 years. Route 1 payback is best; Route 3 barely meets the 3-year target.

brainstorming.prompt: Your client has identified that attracting business travelers will be key to long-term growth and profitability. Please brainstorm some ideas on how your client can increase business travelers in the next 3 years.

categories.name: In-flight Amenities
ideas: Extra legroom and business class cabins (lower price sensitivity)

categories.name: External Partnerships
ideas: Preferred status with Concur and other corporate booking sites
Alliance networks with smaller regional airlines for continuous service

categories.name: Flight Structure
ideas: Early morning and late afternoon time slots to accommodate business schedules

recommendation: No single 'right' route – the case tests ability to handle ambiguity. A strong answer weighs both quantitative (CM, payback period) and qualitative (growth potential, risk, competition, setup time) factors against the client's goal of taking operating margin positive within 3 years.

Route 1 (SEA-MINN) offers the fastest payback (8 months) and lowest risk, but the lowest annual CM and growth potential. Route 2 (FAY-DALL) offers the highest annual CM and fastest setup, but carries high disruption risk. Route 3 (NYC-DC) has the longest setup and barely meets the payback threshold, despite medium growth.
risks: Competitive activity at destination airport – possibility of a price war
Pending local legislation at destination city – could prevent or hinder monopolistic activity or make airline travel prohibitively expensive
Decrease in passenger interest in destination cities
next_steps: Develop regulatory and operational planning schedule to implement the chosen route
